subject.title: fix(browser): use public ssrf runtime import in CDP proxy bypass

question: Should the canonical fix preserve owner-scoped private `ssrf-runtime-internal` access for Browser/Ollama, or intentionally promote these SSRF/proxy-bypass helpers into the public `ssrf-runtime` SDK contract?
rationale: The import-only PR is incomplete, and the obvious ways to complete it either preserve a private owner boundary or expand public SDK access to security-sensitive helper functions.

options.title: Preserve owner-scoped helper access
options.body: Fix the packaged Browser/Ollama load path through the existing private bundled-plugin owner mechanism or another narrow private seam.

options.title: Approve public SDK promotion
options.body: Expose the helpers from `ssrf-runtime` only with explicit SDK/security approval, docs, replacement guardrails, and package smoke proof.

options.title: Pick a canonical sibling or replacement
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers choose one of the broader sibling PRs or a new replacement branch as the canonical repair.

recommendation.title: Preserve owner-scoped helper access
recommendation.body: Fix the packaged Browser/Ollama load path through the existing private bundled-plugin owner mechanism or another narrow private seam.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged the relevant private-boundary PRs and authored adjacent owner-registry/package-boundary commits, making him the best routing candidate for this SDK/security choice.
